scope: Authored task recipes linked to generated method metadata; not an exhaustive list of all possible procedures.

attach.purpose: Attach to the exact operator-selected ETABS process and prove identity before reading.
attach.status: Implemented getter host; each live target still needs its own identity and operation scope.
prerequisites: Selected PID plus start time, executable/runtime fingerprint and expected model; use the maintained lease and supervised STA broker.
steps: Discover processes without API calls and select the exact target.
Use GetObjectProcess, then read version, filename, present/database units and lock state through the existing host.
Bind the current target and preflight state; run only the selected registered getter profile.
Compare postflight state and release the worker-owned COM references and lease.
checks: GetPresentUnits returns an enum directly; do not decode it as status.
A filename or lock flag does not prove an unsaved in-memory model is clean.
Never attach to an arbitrary active instance as a fallback.

overview.purpose: Read lightweight model counts, stories, sections, cases and combinations before choosing acquisition scope.
overview.status: Implemented; retained installed scope recorded in etabs-bounded-acquisition receipt.
prerequisites: Valid exact target and inspection getter profile; bounded overview request.
steps: Dispatch the existing OverviewWorker request.
Read metadata/counts and name lists through EtabsInspectionReader overviewOnly.
Project and retain the overview artifact with source/journal hashes; request geometry or forces only when the next action needs them.
checks: Overview proves neither geometry nor forces nor beam-design support.
Respect count-zero/null-array results rather than inventing a row.

geometry.purpose: Acquire frame identities and geometry for selected members without fetching all force results.
geometry.status: Implemented context capture; detailed support/topology interpretation remains profile-specific.
prerequisites: Valid target; explicit geometry need; context identity bound to later force requests.
steps: Reuse EtabsContextCapture to read GetAllFrames once.
Preserve frame unique names, labels, stories, endpoints, sections and source coordinates.
Project/cache by exact context identity; use member/point getters only for details the next operation requires.
checks: Object and element identities are different; meshed points may not appear among physical endpoints.
Local axes, insertion offsets and physical faces must remain explicit.
Do not use geometry-only data as a complete support or design model.

materials.purpose: Resolve assigned sections, concrete and reinforcement properties with explicit provenance.
materials.status: Existing getters and decoders cover declared profiles; presence of other section methods does not extend design support.
prerequisites: Current member/context identity; declared section and engineering applicability profile.
steps: Read assigned section and any auto-select list.
Resolve its type before the corresponding shape getter.
Read concrete and separate longitudinal/transverse rebar materials.
Retain original properties and unit basis; keep proposed defaults separate from source facts.
checks: A rectangular decoder cannot silently handle every available section type.
GetRebarBeam describes section reinforcement settings; do not treat them as a completed design.

forces.purpose: Read member or batch frame-force rows efficiently from already available analysis results.
forces.status: Implemented member/batch/group paths; installed evidence applies only to retained scopes.
prerequisites: Current target/context, already-finished source results, explicit member/case/combination scope and observable output settings.
steps: Use the existing force request, selecting the smallest member/batch scope needed.
Read status, selected output cases/combinations and result options through the force getter profile.
Call FrameForce through the retained member/bulk/group implementation for that scope.
Validate count and parallel arrays, preserve complete signed rows, normalize units offline and compare postflight state.
checks: Use ItemTypeElm and Name together; group, object, element and selection have different meanings.
Do not combine independent extrema into a synthetic action row.
Do not change output selections on an attached session; caller state is a prerequisite.
Count API calls and requested rows before optimizing; reuse accepted context/definitions, not stale result epochs.

tables.purpose: Discover and read available database tables with their actual field schemas.
tables.status: Existing retained bulk table path; arbitrary table keys and schemas still require qualification.
prerequisites: Valid target, already-observed display selections, explicit requested table and row/size bounds.
steps: Read available table keys and emptiness/status metadata.
Read fields and units for the exact selected key and table version.
Use the display-array getter for in-memory reads, retaining field order and row count.
Decode only the observed qualified schema and retain per-table failure status.
checks: Display-table selection differs from Results.Setup selection.
GetTableForDisplayCSVFile writes an external file despite its Get prefix.
Do not infer a SQLite export method; inspect the installed API surface and retained export contract.

create_model.purpose: Plan an owned model creation procedure from exact installed method contracts.
create_model.status: Documented method sequence only; no new runnable creation workflow or live qualification is delivered by this guide.
prerequisites: Separate owned process/model, explicit creation scope and engineering inputs; never apply this sequence to the attached user session.
steps: Create the owned application with the installed helper contract and start it.
Initialize the model with explicit units and create a blank model.
Define materials/sections/load patterns, then geometry and assignments in dependency order.
Read back definitions and save to a new owned path; analysis is a separate stage.
checks: This is a discovery recipe, not permission or a production runner.
Consult installed help for every required/default parameter, unit, constraint and return contract.

owned_reanalysis.purpose: Plan section changes and analysis on a separately owned copy.
owned_reanalysis.status: Future owned-copy milestone; methods are inventoried but this guide does not implement or qualify the lifecycle.
prerequisites: Saved checkpoint, non-existing owned copy destination, owned process and explicit reviewed change set; existing owned-copy authority/evidence gates apply.
steps: Create and open the owned copy in the owned application.
Capture the baseline, unlock only the owned model as required, apply exact section changes and read them back.
Choose the authorized case dependency closure and run analysis.
Read statuses and fresh force results, bind the new epoch, then save/report only within the accepted stage.
checks: Never promote an attached user session into an owned one.
No cFile.Close or proven solver cancellation/progress method is supplied by this installed inventory.
Worker timeout does not prove ETABS stopped solving; do not automatically replay.

concrete_design.purpose: Plan concrete-design configuration, execution and diagnostic result comparison on an owned model.
concrete_design.status: Method discovery and future owned lifecycle; does not imply engineering or installed design qualification.
prerequisites: Owned analyzed model and explicit design code/preferences/overwrites, combinations, section/rebar identity and current result epoch.
steps: Read or explicitly configure design code and strength combinations within the owned stage.
Run concrete design only after prerequisites pass.
Read availability, design section and beam summary with exact item type and row semantics.
Compare like-for-like cases/stations/units and preserve warnings and design provenance.
checks: GetComboStrength is a missing maintained candidate: do not call it or infer it from SetComboStrength; the future implementation must resolve its evidence need explicitly.
An available summary or comparison is not engineering approval.
